articles.title: India's First Lock Museum Is Coming To THIS City & Here's What You Can Expect
articles.content: Home / India / Trending / India’s First Lock Museum Is Coming To THIS City & Here’s What You Can Expect India is home to thousands of museums that showcase its civilisation, rich history, art, culture and heritage. Now, the country is all set to get its first Lock Museum! by Ashmeet Guliani Updated: October 04, 2026 5:09 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Aligarh, Wikipedia/Whispyhistory and Canva Pro/Vince Barnes (Representative Image) We come bearing some amazing news! India is all set to get its first “Lock Museum” in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh. The state government has approved nearly ₹37 crore for the project. The museum will be developed as a heritage and tourist spot, attracting both locals and foreigners. Here’s what we know so far. India To Get Its 1st Lock Museum In Aligarh India is home to thousands of museums that showcase its civilisation, rich history, art, culture and heritage. Now, the country is all set to get its first “Lock Museum” in Aligarh . According to The Times of India, the Uttar Pradesh government has approved nearly ₹37 crore for the project and has released around ₹10 crore as the first instalment. The museum will showcase the evolution of locks from the Vedic era to modern digital and cyber-locking systems. In addition to that, the museum also aims to shed light on Aligarh’s lock-making industry and provide local manufacturers with a space to display their products to visitors and buyers. The construction of the museum is likely to take around 18 to 24 months. India’s first Lock Museum will feature several sections. They will showcase the history and development of locking systems. Also Read: Humanoid Robots, T-Rex & Eiffel Tower— All Made Of Chocolate! Inside China’s Chocolate Museum Museum To Feature Cafeteria, Workshops And More That’s not all. According to The Times of India, this museum will also feature souvenir shops, a children’s play area, a cafeteria, an auditorium, workshops and function halls. The project is planned both as a tourist attraction and a big platform for the local industry of Aligarh. Visitors to the museum will have so much to look at and learn about Aligarh’s lock manufacturers. You would like to know that the city’s lock industry dates back more than a century. This museum aims to bring this industrial history under one roof. Would you ever like to visit a lock museum to learn about its history in India? articles.title: Museum of Word: Kolkata's new home for India's linguistic heritage - The Week
articles.content: India's first Museum of Word has opened at Belvedere House in Kolkata, offering an immersive journey through the history of language and communication. The museum features nine thematic galleries that utilize interactive displays, sound installations, and digital elements to explore the evolution of human expression, from ancient symbols to contemporary forms. It highlights India's rich linguistic diversity, the cultural significance of its many languages, and the importance of preserving this heritage for future generations. The museum is designed to be dynamic, evolving alongside the languages it showcases. The museum features nine thematic galleries that utilize interactive displays, sound installations, and digital elements to explore the evolution of human expression, from ancient symbols to contemporary forms. It highlights India's rich linguistic diversity, the cultural significance of its many languages, and the importance of preserving this heritage for future generations. The museum is designed to be dynamic, evolving alongside the languages it showcases. Before you hear a single word, you notice the silence. A long driveway shaded by old rain trees leads to Belvedere House, in a quieter corner of Kolkata. The 18th-century mansion has housed the National Library of India since 1948. Alongside the library’s vast collection of books, it now holds a museum devoted to something far more elusive: the story of words and languages. Inaugurated by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in July, the Museum of Word is the first of its kind in India. Developed by the ministry of culture at the National Library, it traces human communication from early sounds and symbols to scripts, literature, oral traditions and contemporary forms of expression. Nothing here is arranged in conventional rows. Words and alphabets hang overhead, screens light up in the darker galleries, voices emerge from installations, and visitors are encouraged to touch, listen and watch. The museum is less about looking at language than entering its world. articles.title: Katra-Banihal Rail Section Clears 100 kmph Speed Milestone - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Katra-Banihal Rail Section Clears 100 kmph Speed Milestone Breaking News Katra-Banihal Rail Section Clears 100 kmph Speed Milestone By Urban Acres October 3, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Katra-Banihal rail section in Jammu and Kashmir has raised its maximum permissible train speed to 100 kmph, with a Vande Bharat Express completing a test run across the Chenab Railway Bridge and Anji Khad Railway Bridge at the new speed. The operational change marks a significant milestone for the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Railway Link (USBRL) project. The speed enhancement was carried out on the 111-km Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section of Northern Railway’s Jammu division after prescribed safety conditions were completed, railway officials said. The earlier maximum permissible speed was 75 kmph across the full section, although different limits applied to separate parts of the route. “The maximum permissible speed on the 111-km-long Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Banihal section has been increased from 75 kmph to 100 kmph,” Senior Divisional Commercial Manager Uchit Singhal said, according to the Times of India report. Vande Bharat Express Train No. 26401/26404 crossed the world’s highest railway bridge over the Chenab River and India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge at Anji at 100 kmph during the test. The Railway Ministry approved the speed increase after the required safety checks were completed in August, officials said. Before the change, trains could operate at up to 85 kmph on the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra-Sangaldan section and 75 kmph on the Sangaldan-Banihal section. The revised limit is expected to reduce travel time between Katra and Banihal and support smoother train operations along the USBRL route. The Katra-Banihal section is a crucial part of the railway project intended to connect the Kashmir Valley with the rest of the country by rail. The route passes through the Pir Panjal and lower Himalayan ranges, where the railway line crosses deep valleys, steep mountain slopes and major rivers while navigating complex geological formations. Its infrastructure includes long tunnels, high-level bridges and specialised railway systems. The section has 33 tunnels, along with the Chenab Railway Bridge near Reasi and the Anji Khad Railway Bridge. The Chenab bridge is described as the world’s highest railway bridge, while the Anji structure is India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge. The speed milestone also places the focus on the operational challenge of running trains through one of India’s most technically demanding railway corridors. Raising the permissible speed required safety compliance across a route where infrastructure, terrain and train operations are closely linked. The Katra-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express was flagged off from Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra on June 6, 2025. The latest test run follows that service milestone and represents an operational enhancement on the wider USBRL network. Railway officials said the revised speed limit would improve the movement of trains on the Katra-Banihal section.
